title: Order of operations
subtitle: Use BIDMAS to decide which operation to complete first.

explanation.title: Why does order matter?
paragraphs: A calculation can contain more than one operation.
For example, in 3 + 4 × 2, multiplying first gives 3 + 8 = 11. Adding first would give 14.
Mathematicians use an agreed order of operations so that every calculation has one correct answer.
BIDMAS stands for Brackets, Indices, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.
key_points: Calculate indices next, including powers and roots.
Division and multiplication have equal priority, so work from left to right.
Addition and subtraction have equal priority, so work from left to right.
Complete one operation at a time and rewrite the calculation after each step.

steps.title: Complete the brackets
steps.text: Work out any calculations inside brackets before anything outside them.

steps.title: Calculate the indices
steps.text: Work out powers and roots, such as 3² or √25.

steps.title: Complete division and multiplication
steps.text: Division and multiplication have equal priority. Work from left to right.

steps.title: Complete addition and subtraction
steps.text: Addition and subtraction also have equal priority. Work from left to right.

steps.title: Rewrite the calculation
steps.text: Replace only the operation you have completed with its answer, then decide what comes next.

interactive.title: Complete the calculation map
interactive.intro: Choose which operation should be completed next, then calculate it. The full expression will remain visible while each completed step is added to the map.

worked_examples.title: Calculate 18 ÷ 3 × 2
steps: Division and multiplication have equal priority.
The division is further left, so calculate 18 ÷ 3 first.

worked_examples.title: Calculate 5 + (12 − 4) ÷ 2² × 3
steps: Division and multiplication have equal priority, so work from left to right: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

worked_examples.title: Calculate 3(√25 − 2)
steps: Calculate the root inside the brackets: √25 = 5.
A number directly beside a bracket means multiplication.

question_bank.title: Practise order of operations
question_bank.intro: Choose a difficulty and generate a new set of questions involving brackets, indices, equal-priority operations and mixed calculations.
